clue.text: Endless story family doctor developed into topic

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the last letter of the next word goes

parts.note: a story is a tale
your family are your kin
a GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A family doctor's tale, trimmed short, is worked up into a subject for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family doctor' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces: family and doctor. Story loses its last letter, and only the word 'into' is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking point is a subject that people discuss, so it is a synonym for a topic of conversation.

clue.text: Wrong test for the oddly reliable person

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the preceding words are put in a strange order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these four words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone dependable sits an inappropriate exam, which seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; the signal is 'oddly', which also tempts you to take odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for someone who gives steady support in hard times, whom others can depend upon.

clue.text: Hurry up and appear with second instrument

parts.note: to look a certain way is to appear so
S is the abbreviation for second
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician is told to get a move on and show up with a backup instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Look sharp is a British idiom, an order to be quick and alert, so it means to get moving fast.

clue.text: Home and dry, having no heart for form of racing

indicators.note: a word with no heart has lost its central letter, so the middle of the word before goes

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
taken as written, before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: A horse that is home and dry has won, yet lacks heart for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home and dry' is an idiom for safely finished, but here it splits: home, then dry with its middle letter gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy is short for IndyCar, the American open-wheel motor-racing series, so it names a kind of racing.

clue.text: Enormous worry newspaper raised with trade union article

indicators.note: in a down clue, something raised is read bottom to top, so the first two pieces run backwards

parts.note: to nag is to worry at someone
a rag is a slang name for a low-quality newspaper
TU is the abbreviation for trade union
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A huge worry is raised in the press alongside a story about trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantuan, after Rabelais's giant Gargantua, is a synonym for huge or vast in size.

clue.text: Egg-shaped ornament initially empty

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word before it, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of ornament
something void is empty

explanation.surface: An egg-shaped decoration turns out to be hollow at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid comes from Latin ovum, egg, and describes a solid shape like that of an egg.

clue.text: Union rebel sighs, ordered to show sociability

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a sequence, so the letters before are arranged anew

parts.note: all fifteen letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A union rebel sighs when told to be friendly to colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as being commanded, but it is the signal to put the letters in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbourliness is friendly, helpful behaviour toward people living nearby, a kind of sociability.

clue.text: Mild pressure applied to edge of Bakewell tart

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: the edge of a word is its outermost part, here the final letter of the place name

parts.note: the final letter of Bakewell
tart means sharp-tasting, sour

explanation.surface: Gentle pressure is pressed onto the rim of a Bakewell tart, a British almond-and-jam pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bakewell tart' is a well-known British pastry, but tart here is an adjective meaning sour, separate from Bakewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and not easily upset, so it describes a mild, gentle temperament.

clue.text: Great footballer occupied by work for human beings

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it sitting inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A legendary footballer is kept busy with a job for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: People is the plural word for humans in general, so it equals human beings.

clue.text: A door well designed for truck

indicators.note: something designed has been planned and made up, so the letters before are laid out in a new pattern

parts.note: all nine letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A well-designed door is meant for a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-loader is a lorry with a low flat bed for carrying heavy machinery, a kind of truck.

clue.text: Have home next to old green

indicators.note: next to means the pieces sit side by side, with the later clue word placed first

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
to live somewhere is to have your home there

explanation.surface: Someone sets up house beside an old village green.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a dull yellowish green, named after the colour of unripe olives.

clue.text: Plant receiving a gentle touch

indicators.note: something receiving another thing takes it in, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: cress is a salad plant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener tends a plant with a light hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' looks like part of the phrase 'a gentle touch', but it is the letter that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a soft, affectionate stroke, a tender gentle touch.

clue.text: Solid vessel in trouble

parts.note: hard means solid, firm
a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: A sturdy ship finds itself in difficulties at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or adversity, a state of difficulty that matches trouble as a noun.

clue.text: Musical song's aim is varied

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so the letters before are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters are the raw material, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A critic notes that a show tune's purpose keeps changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Saigon is the Boublil and Schönberg stage musical set during the Vietnam War.

clue.text: If teased badly, time to be despondent

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters before are jumbled

parts.note: eight letters taken as written, then shuffled
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone mocked cruelly decides it is time to feel low.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeatist expects failure and gives up hope, so the word as an adjective means despondent or pessimistic.

clue.text: Range covered by disco perhaps

indicators.note: something covered by words lies inside them, so the letters run across the following phrase

parts.note: the letters run from the end of disco into the start of perhaps

explanation.surface: A DJ's repertoire is perhaps bounded by disco music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like it marks disco as an example, but it is just the second half of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope is the extent or breadth of something, which is what range means as a noun.

clue.text: Wild horse, pure one with unusual power

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters after are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A wild, thoroughbred horse seems to have extraordinary strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like the letter I or O to add, but it begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero is a comic-book character with extraordinary abilities, someone gifted with abnormal powers.

clue.text: In distress, divided

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are the same two-word phrase: one figurative, about feelings, one literal, about slicing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut up is British informal for being very upset, and something cut up has been sliced into parts.

clue.text: Stick around with permission

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around
leave means permission, as in by your leave

explanation.surface: Someone stays put, having been granted leave to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but it supplies a letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave to something is to cling or adhere, so the verb shares the sense of stick fast.

clue.text: Fearful about agent, turned and ran away

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: fearful means frightened

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word just before is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent, short for representative

explanation.surface: A frightened spy spun round and fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' seems to join 'and ran away' as action, but it reverses the agent. Scarper is British slang for run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for bolting or fleeing quickly, so the past tense matches ran away.

clue.text: Democrat studies fears

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician examines what frightens voters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread something is to be very afraid of it, so the verb form matches fears.

clue.text: Final net value resolved

indicators.note: something resolved has been broken down and worked out afresh, so the letters before are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: An accountant settles the last figure for net value.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual describes what happens in the end, after a process, so it is a synonym for ultimate.

clue.text: Number on love right for singer

parts.note: ten is a number
love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O; in a down clue, on means placed above
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A number about love is just right for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' suggests a song, but here it gives a plain numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male vocalist with a high voice range, so the word names a kind of singer.

clue.text: Stoat's hesitation in front of pit

indicators.note: in front of means one piece leads and the next follows directly behind it

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating in speech
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A stoat pauses uncertainly at the mouth of a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the name for the stoat in its white winter coat, so the two words name one animal.

clue.text: Powder used by hospital cleaner

indicators.note: something used by the following words is carried within them, so the letters lie in that phrase

parts.note: the letters run from the end of hospital into the start of cleaner

explanation.surface: A hospital cleaner sprinkles powder on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc, or talcum, is a soft mineral ground fine and used as a body powder.

clue.text: One not using animal products for example in vehicle

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first piece goes into the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Someone who avoids animal goods, say, travels in a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' looks like a link phrase introducing an illustration, but it supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats and uses nothing derived from animals, such as meat, dairy, eggs or leather.

clue.text: Serious post in place in Kent

parts.note: grave means serious, solemn
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: A solemn job posting in a county in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' reads as a noun, a job, but it is the verb meaning to dispatch. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a town on the south bank of the Thames estuary in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Station group angry after tea

indicators.note: after means placed behind, so the earlier clue words follow the last word's letters

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a ring is a group, such as a gang
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: At a railway station a group gets annoyed after stopping for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea, from Chinese; it goes first even though tea comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Charing Cross is a mainline railway terminus and Tube stop in central London.
